Revelation Beam (focuses light to reveal hidden things)
Voice Amplification (amplifies her singing, making it carry for miles)
Dawn's Crown (the comb's light protects her from darkness-based attacks)

companion.name: Jīn Jī
companion.description: He is the first light of dawn made flesh, a creature of such radiant beauty that his crowing actually summons the sun. Jīn Jī is the Golden Rooster, about the size of a large eagle, his form a breathtaking symphony of gold and crimson that seems to hold captured sunlight within every feather. His head is crowned with a magnificent comb of living flame that flickers gently, never burning, always warm—a crown of fire that pulses with the rhythm of dawn itself. His eyes are pools of molten gold, identical to Chén Xī's own, holding the same eternal warmth and hopeful vigilance that makes all who meet him feel that the night will eventually end. From his beak, curved and sharp, emerges a crow that is not sound but pure light—a beam of gold that pierces darkness and carries hope to the hopeless. His wattles, the red skin beneath his beak, glow with inner fire when he is about to crow, warning all who see that dawn is coming. His body is covered in feathers that shimmer through every shade of gold and crimson imaginable—from pale sunrise gold at his breast to deep blazing crimson at his wingtips, each feather seeming to hold its own tiny flame. The feathers are not soft but firm, each one a tiny blade of light that can deflect darkness and reveal truth. Upon his back, he wears no armor—he needs none—but his feathers are harder than any metal, and his presence alone can dispel shadows and reveal hidden things. His wings are magnificent, spanning wider than a chariot, each primary feather tipped with a tiny sunstone that blazes with light when he flies. When he spreads his wings, they seem to encompass the sky, casting not shadow but radiance, a warm golden light that makes all who stand in it feel safe and hopeful. His tail is a cascade of long, curved feathers that trail behind him like a river of light, each one shimmering with every color of dawn. His legs are strong and scaly, ending in claws of gold that can grip any perch, and when he stands, he stands proud, his chest thrust forward, his head held high, as if challenging the night itself. Jīn Jī's stance is one of eternal vigilance—he perches on Chén Xī's shoulder or on the peak of the highest building, his head cocked, his eyes scanning the horizon for the first hint of darkness. When dawn approaches, he begins to glow, his feathers brightening until he becomes a beacon of light. And when the moment is right, he crows—a sound that is not noise but pure radiance, a beam of golden light that shoots across the sky, awakening the sun and banishing the night. When Chén Xī sings, Jīn Jī accompanies her, his crow harmonizing with her voice to create a music that can calm storms and soothe savage hearts. Together, they are the dawn itself, the promise that no matter how dark the night, morning will always come.
abilities: Dawn's Crow (a crow that dispels darkness and inspires hope)
Golden Flight (flies at incredible speeds, leaving trails of light)
Feather Armor (its feathers are impervious to most damage)
Shared Light (Chén Xī sees everything Jīn Jī sees)

basic_skills.name: Golden Gaze
basic_skills.description: Chén Xī fixes her sunrise gold eyes on a target. The target feels suddenly, inexplicably warm, as if the first light of dawn is touching them. Fear fades, hope rises, and they feel that everything will be alright.

basic_skills.name: Rooster's Crow
basic_skills.description: Jīn Jī crows once, a sound that carries across the battlefield. Allies feel their spirits lift, their courage strengthen, their hope renewed. Enemies feel a strange unease, as if the night is ending and they are not ready for the light.

basic_skills.name: Dawn's Step
basic_skills.description: She dissolves into a shaft of golden light and reappears elsewhere, leaving a trail of warmth and radiance behind her. Where she reappears, shadows flee and hope returns.

passive_skill.name: Aura of Eternal Dawn
passive_skill.description: Chén Xī radiates an aura of warm, hopeful light at all times. All within range feel their spirits lifting, their fears easing, their hope returning. The lost feel guided; the hopeless feel inspired; the dark-hearted feel uncomfortable, as if their darkness is being exposed. This aura does not fight—it illuminates, and in that illumination, darkness cannot stand.

special_skills.name: Dawn's Radiance
special_skills.description: Chén Xī raises her arms and releases a wave of golden-crimson light that washes over the entire battlefield. Allies are healed and inspired; enemies are dazzled and disoriented. Hidden things are revealed; dark places are illuminated. For a moment, everywhere is dawn.

special_skills.name: Song of Homecoming
special_skills.description: She sings—a wordless melody of such pure beauty that all who hear it feel an overwhelming sense of home, of safety, of belonging. Enemies find their aggression cooling, their desire to fight fading; allies find their courage strengthening, their purpose clarifying. The lost find their way; the hopeless find hope.

special_skills.name: Light's Embrace
special_skills.description: She calls upon the Golden Comb, and golden light wraps around each ally like a warm embrace. The light protects them from harm, heals their wounds, and guides them through darkness. Where they walk, shadows flee and hope follows.

ultimate_skill.name: Crimson Herald's Judgment: The Dawn That Cannot Be Denied
ultimate_skill.description: Chén Xī's golden eyes blaze with the light of a thousand sunrises, and Jīn Jī rises into the air, his wings spreading wide, his comb blazing with living flame. Chén Xī raises Dawn's Call Blades and touches the Golden Comb, and they all become one with the light. She speaks a single, radiant word: 'Dawn.' In that moment, golden-crimson light explodes from her, washing over the entire battlefield. It is not a weapon—it is a revelation. Every shadow is banished. Every hidden thing is revealed. Every dark thought is illuminated. Enemies find their darkness exposed, their evil intentions laid bare, their hatred revealed for what it is. But in that same light, they also see their own humanity, their own capacity for good, their own hope. Allies are healed completely, their spirits lifted, their purpose renewed. The battlefield becomes not a place of conflict, but a place of awakening. When the light fades, the battle is over—not because anyone was defeated, but because everyone has seen the dawn. Enemies lay down their weapons, not in surrender, but in recognition. Allies embrace, not in victory, but in hope. Chén Xī stands at the center, Jīn Jī beside her, both glowing with the light of eternal dawn. She has not defeated anyone. She has simply reminded them that dawn always comes. She is Chén Xī. She is the Crimson Herald. And the night is over.

title: The Iron Fang • Guardian Dog of the Northern Pass
nickname: She Who Never Abandons, Never Forgets, Never Wavers
lore: In the snowy passes of the northern frontier, where the Great Wall winds like a sleeping dragon and the cold bites deeper than any blade, there lived a woman named Xūnyì who was known by a different name before she earned her title. She was simply called 'the dog girl' by the soldiers at the garrison—a name spoken with affection, not cruelty, for they had watched her grow from a feral child into a young woman who seemed more wolf than human. She had been found as a baby in the wreckage of a caravan that had been attacked by raiders, the sole survivor protected by the body of a massive wolf-dog who had died shielding her. The soldiers took her in, but she never quite became one of them. She preferred the company of the garrison's dogs, learned their language, their ways, their loyalties. By the time she was ten, she could communicate with any canine, understand their warnings, and fight alongside them as if they shared a single mind. By sixteen, she was the garrison's best scout, her nose as keen as any hound's, her hearing sharp enough to catch a whisper from a mile away, her loyalty to the soldiers who had raised her absolute. She had no family, no name, no past—only the present moment and the people she had chosen to protect. The great blizzard came without warning, a white wall of death that descended from the mountains and trapped a group of children from a nearby village in the high passes. The soldiers wanted to wait for the storm to pass, but Xūnyì knew the children would not survive that long. She did not ask permission. She simply gathered the garrison's dogs—a pack of fifteen mongrels and mastiffs who loved her as she loved them—and walked into the storm. For three days, no word came. The soldiers assumed she had perished. But on the fourth morning, as the storm finally broke, they saw a line of figures emerging from the white—Xūnyì, leading the pack, and behind them, every single child, alive, stumbling but walking, guided through the blizzard by a woman who refused to let them die. She had lost three of her dogs to the cold, wrapped around children to keep them warm. She herself had frostbite on her cheeks and fingers, wounds that would scar forever. But she had saved them all. When she reached the garrison gates, she collapsed, and the dogs who survived lay around her, guarding her as she had guarded them. That night, as she lay recovering, the Dog Spirit appeared to her—not as a beast, but as a magnificent wolf-dog of living steel and moonlight, its fur the color of burnished iron, its eyes glowing with loyal blue light, its presence radiating the truth that true loyalty never wavers. 'You have learned what dogs know in their bones,' it said. 'That family is not blood—it is choice. That protection is not duty—it is love. That loyalty is not conditional—it is absolute. Will you carry my mark and become the Iron Fang, the one who never abandons, never forgets, never wavers?' Xūnyì looked at the spirit, then at the dogs sleeping around her, then at the garrison where her family waited. 'Will I still be able to protect them?' she asked. The spirit's eyes blazed with blue light. 'You will protect them all, everywhere, forever.' Xūnyì accepted. Her body, already lean and powerful from years of running with dogs, refined into something more than human. Her simple clothes transformed into armor of steel-grey and loyal brown. Her scars, badges of honor, remained—a reminder of those she had lost and those she had saved. And from the mountains, padding with the silent grace of a wolf, came Tiě Quǎn, the Iron Dog—a magnificent creature of living steel and moonlight, its coat the color of burnished iron with white markings like fresh snow, its eyes glowing with loyal blue light, its presence radiating absolute fidelity. It walked to her and lay its head in her lap, and they became one in purpose. Now, Xūnyì roams the realms as the Iron Fang, the guardian who never wavers, the protector who never abandons. She does not seek glory—she seeks those who are lost, who are alone, who have no one else to guard them. She is the scout who sees danger before it arrives, the warrior who stands between the innocent and the darkness, the friend who never leaves. And always, beside her, Tiě Quǎn walks, their bond a testament to the truth that loyalty is the strongest force in the universe.
description: Xūnyì is the embodiment of unwavering loyalty and fierce protection, a woman whose very presence makes the vulnerable feel safe and the wicked feel hunted. She stands at a powerful five feet nine inches, her form the epitome of lean, functional strength—broad shoulders built for endurance, a narrow waist that twists with predator grace, full high breasts that curve against her leather and steel armor, hips that move with the fluid power of a hunting wolf, and long, powerful legs that have run through blizzards and never stopped. Her body is not the sculpted perfection of a warrior who trains for show, but the lean, efficient build of one who lives with dogs, runs with packs, and fights with tooth and claw. Every muscle is defined, every line speaks of purpose, every scar tells a story of protection given and received. Her skin is warm and weathered, with a healthy, sun-kissed undertone, marked with the faint white lines of old scars—the frostbite scars on her cheeks and fingers are the most prominent, badges of honor from the night she saved the children. Her face is strikingly beautiful in a wild, untamed way—high, sharp cheekbones that could cut the wind, a straight nose with flared nostrils that constantly scent the air for danger, full lips the color of warm terracotta, usually set in a calm, watchful line that betrays nothing of the fierce loyalty within. But her eyes are her most captivating feature: they are large, almond-shaped pools of warm, loyal brown, holding an eternal vigilance that has watched through blizzards and never blinked. When she looks at you, you feel not judged, but protected—as if someone has finally decided that you are worth guarding, and nothing will make them leave. Her hair is a wild, practical mane of steel-grey, shot through with streaks of loyal brown and the white of winter snow, cropped short and functional, often matted and tangled from days in the wilderness, but always clean, always cared for. It frames her sharp features like a wolf's ruff, untamed and beautiful. On her forehead, she wears no mark—her loyalty is written in her scars, not on her skin. Her ears are slightly pointed, more canine than human, a gift from her years with the pack, and they twitch constantly, catching every sound. Her attire is a masterpiece of functional ferocity, designed for a woman who moves through wilderness and war with equal ease. She wears a form-fitting leather jerkin of loyal brown, reinforced with steel-grey plates at the shoulders, chest, and arms. The jerkin is sleeveless, leaving her powerful arms bare, and cut low enough at the neck to reveal the beginning of her athletic cleavage and the simple leather cord she wears. Over this, she wears a short cloak of wolf fur—not taken, but shed by her pack—warm and practical, clasped at her throat with a steel pin shaped like a wolf's head. A wide belt of braided leather and steel links cinches her narrow waist, from which hang her weapons and a small pouch containing dried meat for her pack. On her lower body, she wears sturdy leather pants of loyal brown, reinforced at the knees with steel-grey plates, tucked into high boots of the same leather, soled for silent movement through any terrain. On her arms, she wears steel bracers etched with the names of every dog she has lost. On her wrists, simple leather cords, each one a promise to a pack member that she will never abandon them. Around her neck hangs a simple leather cord with a single, worn dog tooth—the tooth of the wolf-dog who died protecting her as an infant, her only connection to a past she never knew. On her fingers, she wears no rings—they would catch on fur and leather—but her hands themselves are adorned with the calluses and scars of a life lived protecting others. In her strong, loyal hands, she carries her legendary weapons: Fang of the Pack and the Unbreakable Collar. Fang of the Pack is a pair of heavy, single-edged broadswords, their blades forged from steel-grey metal that seems to absorb light, their hilts wrapped in worn brown leather that has molded perfectly to her grip. Each sword is slightly curved, designed for powerful, relentless slashing, and when she wields them, they trail a faint brown and white aura that strengthens allies near her. The Unbreakable Collar is not a weapon in the traditional sense—it is a simple leather collar with a steel tag, which she wears around her own neck, a symbol of her bond to those she protects. When activated, it can create a protective link between her and any ally she chooses, allowing her to share their pain, to know their location, to be there when they need her. Beside her always pads her spirit animal and companion: Tiě Quǎn, the Iron Dog. The dog is magnificent, standing as tall as a wolf at the shoulder, its coat a stunning blend of burnished iron-grey and pure white, each hair seeming to hold captured moonlight. Its eyes are glowing pools of loyal blue, identical to the light that sometimes shines in Xūnyì's own, and its presence radiates absolute fidelity. It wears armor of steel-grey plates on its chest and shoulders, light and functional, leaving its powerful legs free for running. Its teeth are steel-capped, its claws sheathed in iron, and its growl can shake the courage of any enemy. Tiě Quǎn is not merely a pet—it is an extension of Xūnyì's will, her scout, her shield, her sister. They hunt together, fight together, protect together, and their bond is so deep that they share pain, share joy, share purpose. Xūnyì moves through the world like a wolf on the hunt—silent, watchful, utterly devoted to her pack. She is Xūnyì, and she has never abandoned anyone who needed her.

story.part1: Xūnyì's earliest memory is not of a face, but of fur—the warmth of a wolf-dog's body, the rhythm of its breathing, the protective weight of it curled around her tiny form. She was found in the wreckage of a caravan, the sole survivor, protected by a dog who had died to save her. She never knew her parents, never knew her name. The soldiers called her 'the dog girl,' and it became her identity.
story.part2: She grew up with the garrison's dogs, learning their language, their ways, their loyalties. She could communicate with any canine by the time she was ten, understand their warnings, fight alongside them as if they shared a single mind. The soldiers accepted her, loved her even, but she always felt more comfortable with the pack.
story.part3: By sixteen, she was the garrison's best scout. Her nose was as keen as any hound's, her hearing sharp enough to catch a whisper from a mile away. She could track anything through any terrain, and her loyalty to the soldiers who had raised her was absolute. She had found her pack.
story.part4: The blizzard came without warning, trapping a group of children in the high passes. The soldiers wanted to wait for the storm to pass, but Xūnyì knew the children would not survive. She gathered the garrison's dogs—fifteen mongrels and mastiffs who loved her as she loved them—and walked into the storm.
story.part5: For three days, she led them through the white hell. Three dogs died, wrapped around children to keep them warm. Xūnyì lost fingers to frostbite, earned scars on her cheeks that would never fade. But on the fourth morning, she emerged from the storm with every child alive. She collapsed at the garrison gates, and the surviving dogs lay around her, guarding her.
story.part6: That night, the Dog Spirit appeared, offering her a greater purpose: to become the Iron Fang, the guardian who never wavers, the protector who never abandons. Xūnyì accepted, for she had been protecting her pack her whole life.
story.part7: Now, Xūnyì roams the realms with Tiě Quǎn beside her, seeking those who are lost, who are alone, who have no one else to guard them. She is the scout who sees danger before it arrives, the warrior who stands between the innocent and the darkness, the friend who never leaves. She is Xūnyì, and she has never abandoned anyone who needed her.

companion.name: Tiě Quǎn
companion.description: He pads through the world like a shadow with purpose, his massive form a living testament to the power of loyalty and the strength of those who never abandon their pack. Tiě Quǎn is the Iron Dog, standing as tall as a wolf at the shoulder, his body a breathtaking fusion of living muscle and enchanted steel that gleams with the light of a thousand faithful hearts. His head is broad and noble, with eyes that glow with loyal blue light—pools of warm, faithful light that hold the memory of every pack member he has ever protected. His ears are large and constantly pricked forward, catching every sound, every whimper, every cry for help from miles away. His muzzle is powerful, lined with teeth of steel-capped ivory that can rend armor or gently carry a wounded child to safety. From his neck hangs a heavy iron collar, etched with the names of every dog who died protecting Xūnyì in that blizzard long ago—a memorial worn with pride, each name a reminder of why he fights. His body is covered in a coat that shimmers like burnished iron, each hair seeming to be made of fine metal wire, with patches of pure white on his chest and paws that glow with inner light. The coat is warm to the touch, heated by the furnace of his loyal heart, and it radiates a gentle heat that can warm a freezing traveler or soothe a frightened child. Upon his back and shoulders, he wears magnificent armor of steel-grey plates—light, functional, scarred from countless battles fought in protection of the pack. The armor is etched with images of wolves running together, of packs united, of loyalty made manifest. His legs are powerful and built for endurance, ending in paws with claws of retractable steel that can grip any surface or rend any enemy. His tail is long and bushy, carried high when he is confident, tucked slightly when he is wary, but always ready to wag at the sight of a friend. Tiě Quǎn's stance is one of eternal, watchful readiness—he stands beside Xūnyì, his head level with her hip, his eyes scanning in the opposite direction, ensuring that no threat can approach unseen. When she rests, he lies at her feet, his head on his paws, one eye always open, one ear always listening. When she fights, he fights beside her, their movements synchronized by a bond deeper than thought, each covering the other's blind spots, each drawing strength from the other's presence. His growl is not merely sound—it is a warning that carries the weight of absolute fidelity, a promise that those who threaten his pack will face something they cannot intimidate, cannot bribe, cannot break. And when the battle is done, he licks her wounds, his rough tongue carrying healing warmth, and curls around her, his body a warm fortress against the cold. He is not merely a companion; he is Xūnyì's other self, the physical manifestation of the loyalty that drives her, the proof that some bonds cannot be broken, that some promises last forever.

basic_skills.name: Loyal Gaze

basic_skills.name: Dog's Presence
basic_skills.description: Tiě Quǎn simply stands nearby, his loyal blue eyes watching. All who see him feel safer, stronger, more protected. Enemies feel their courage waver; allies feel their resolve harden.

basic_skills.name: Scent the Wind
basic_skills.description: She lifts her head and scents the air, reading it like a map. In an instant, she knows the location of every enemy, every ally, every hidden danger within range. Nothing can hide from her nose.

passive_skill.name: Aura of Unwavering Protection
passive_skill.description: Xūnyì radiates an aura of absolute, protective loyalty at all times. All within range feel safer, stronger, more protected. Allies find their courage hardened, their resolve strengthened. Enemies find their attacks less effective, their confidence shaken. This aura does not attack—it protects, and in that protection, her pack becomes unbreakable.

special_skills.name: Pack's Embrace

Every ally within range feels a surge of strength and courage, their bonds with each other deepening, their coordination becoming perfect. They fight as one, move as one, protect as one.

special_skills.name: Unyielding Guardian
special_skills.description: She activates the Unbreakable Collar and chooses one ally to protect absolutely. For a duration, any damage that ally would take is instead transferred to Xūnyì, who bears it with unwavering loyalty. She cannot be stopped, cannot be deterred, cannot be moved from her post.

special_skills.name: Hunter's Pursuit
special_skills.description: She marks a target with her scent and begins the hunt. Xūnyì and Tiě Quǎn move as one, tracking the target across any terrain, through any obstacle. Their speed increases with each passing moment, and when they finally catch their prey, their combined attack is devastating.

ultimate_skill.name: Iron Fang's Judgment: The Pack That Never Breaks
ultimate_skill.description: Xūnyì's brown eyes blaze with loyal blue light, and Tiě Quǎn throws back his head and howls—a sound that carries across the realms. Xūnyì raises both Fang of the Pack blades and touches the Unbreakable Collar. She speaks a single, fierce word: 'Pack.' In that moment, brown-white light explodes from her, washing over the entire battlefield. Every ally within range is suddenly, completely connected. They share senses, share strength, share purpose. They move as one, fight as one, protect as one. Enemies find themselves facing not individuals, but a single, unbreakable entity—a pack that cannot be divided, cannot be broken, cannot be defeated. Every attack against one is met by the defense of all. Every strike by one is supported by the strength of all. The pack moves across the battlefield like a single organism, unstoppable, inevitable, eternal. When the light fades, the battle is over. The pack stands together, exhausted but unbroken, their bonds stronger than ever. Xūnyì stands at their center, Tiě Quǎn beside her, both glowing with the light of absolute loyalty. She has not just won a battle—she has reminded them what it means to be a pack. She is Xūnyì. She is the Iron Fang. And the pack never breaks.

title: The Golden Harvest • Bountiful Pig of the Rice Terraces
nickname: She Who Feeds the Hungry and Laughs with the Full Belly
lore: In the emerald-green rice terraces of Yunnan, where mountainsides are carved into staircases of jade and water flows in channels built a thousand years ago, there lived a woman named Fēng Shōu who was known throughout the region for her extraordinary generosity. She was a farmer's widow, neither young nor beautiful by conventional standards, but her presence in any village made people smile. She had a round, cheerful face, arms strong from decades of planting and harvesting, and a laugh that could be heard across three terraces. When her husband died in a landslide, leaving her alone with their small farm, the villagers expected her to struggle, to fade, to eventually sell the land and move away. Instead, Fēng Shōu planted more. She worked from before dawn until after dark, her sturdy body bending and lifting, planting and harvesting, never stopping, never complaining. She grew more rice than her little plot should have been able to produce, and she gave most of it away. To families with hungry children, she gave rice. To neighbors whose crops failed, she gave rice. To passing travelers, to wandering monks, to anyone who crossed her path with an empty belly, she gave rice. The villagers shook their heads. 'You will starve yourself,' they said. 'You cannot give away what you need to survive.' Fēng Shōu would pat her round belly and laugh her wonderful laugh. 'Look at me,' she would say. 'Do I look like I'm starving? The more I give, the more I have. It's a miracle.' And it was, in a way. Her fields never failed. Her harvests never diminished. The more she gave, the more her land produced, as if the earth itself recognized her generosity and responded in kind. The great famine came after three years of drought that turned the terraces to dust and the rivers to trickles. Crops failed across the entire region. Children grew thin, then skeletal, then still. The old died first, then the young, then the strong. Fēng Shōu watched her neighbors starve, watched children she had fed for years grow weak and pale. She gave them everything she had—every grain of rice, every vegetable from her garden, every scrap of food in her home. Within a week, her stores were empty. Within two weeks, she was hungry herself. But still she did not stop. She walked to the fields that had never failed her, now dry and cracked, and she knelt in the dust. She did not pray for rain. She did not pray for food. She prayed for the strength to keep giving, even when she had nothing left to give. As she knelt there, a strange thing happened. The dry earth beneath her hands began to tremble. A single green shoot pushed through the cracked soil, then another, then another. Within minutes, a patch of rice was growing at her feet, not in water but in dust, growing impossibly fast, reaching maturity in moments. Fēng Shōu harvested it and carried it to the village, where she fed the hungriest children. When she returned to the field, more had grown. For the rest of the famine, that one small patch of her land produced enough rice to feed the entire village. No one starved. No one died. When the rains finally returned, the villagers came to her and knelt. 'You are a goddess,' they said. 'You saved us.' Fēng Shōu laughed her wonderful laugh and helped them up. 'I'm no goddess,' she said. 'I'm just a farmer who got lucky. Now come help me plant the real fields.' That night, as she sat alone in her small home, the Pig Spirit appeared to her—not as a fearsome beast, but as a magnificent golden sow with eyes like harvest moons, her body round and warm, her presence radiating abundance and joy. 'You have learned what pigs know in their bones,' it said. 'That abundance is not in hoarding, but in sharing. That the greatest joy is not in having, but in giving. That a full belly and a laughing heart are the greatest treasures. Will you carry my mark and become the Golden Harvest, the one who feeds the hungry and laughs with the full belly?' Fēng Shōu looked at the spirit, then at her empty home, then at the village where children slept with full stomachs for the first time in months. 'Will I still be able to feed them?' she asked. The spirit's eyes blazed with golden light. 'You will feed them all, everywhere, forever.' Fēng Shōu accepted. Her body, already round and warm, refined into something more than human—more beautiful, more radiant, more generous. Her simple clothes transformed into robes of harvest gold and forest green. And from the restored terraces, walking with the patient grace of abundance itself, came Jīn Zhū, the Golden Pig—a magnificent creature of living gold and autumn light, its coat shimmering like ripe grain, its eyes warm pools of harvest gold, its presence radiating joy and plenty. It walked to her and nuzzled her hand, and they became one in purpose. Now, Fēng Shōu roams the realms as the Golden Harvest, the one who feeds the hungry and brings abundance to the barren. She does not fight with violence—she fights with generosity, with joy, with the undeniable truth that there is always enough if we share. She is the farmer who never stops planting, the giver who never runs out, the laugh that makes the world feel lighter. And always, beside her, Jīn Zhū trots, their bond a testament to the truth that abundance grows when shared.
description: Fēng Shōu is the embodiment of generous abundance and joyful plenty, a woman whose very presence makes the world feel richer, warmer, more full of possibility. She stands at a comfortable five feet five inches, her form the epitome of generous curves and maternal warmth—a round, welcoming figure with a soft, full belly that speaks of good meals shared, ample hips that sway with unhurried grace, full high breasts that curve against her golden robes with maternal abundance, and strong, sturdy legs that have walked countless miles through rice terraces. Her body is not the lean form of a warrior, but the healthy, strong figure of one who has worked the land, fed the hungry, and laughed often. Every curve speaks of life lived fully, of abundance shared, of joy embraced. Her skin is warm and golden, with a healthy, sun-kissed glow like ripe grain, smooth and flawless, soft to the touch and radiating warmth. Her face is breathtakingly beautiful in a warm, motherly way—high, cheerful cheekbones that lift when she smiles, a straight nose with a kind curve, full lips the color of ripe apricots, almost always curved in a smile that could mean anything from gentle amusement to uproarious laughter. But her eyes are her most captivating feature: they are large, warm pools of harvest gold, holding an eternal generosity that has fed the hungry and never asked for thanks, an infinite capacity for joy that makes everyone around her feel lighter. When she looks at you, you feel not judged, but welcomed—as if you have finally come home to a place where there will always be enough, and someone is happy to see you. Her hair is a magnificent cascade of deep chestnut brown, shot through with streaks of harvest gold and autumn orange, falling past her shoulders in soft, wavy curls that frame her round, cheerful face. It is often tied back in a practical ponytail, with a few strands always escaping to frame her face, and she sometimes tucks a stalk of rice behind her ear as an ornament. On her forehead, she wears no mark—her generosity is written in her smile, not on her skin. Her attire is a masterpiece of warm abundance, designed for a woman who works the land and feeds the world. She wears a flowing ruqun-style robe of harvest gold silk, embroidered with green and brown thread in patterns of rice stalks, full moon festivals, and dancing pigs. The robe is comfortable and practical, with wide sleeves that can be rolled up for work, and a neckline that reveals the generous swell of her breasts, warm and welcoming rather than provocative. Over this, she wears a shorter jacket of forest green silk, open at the front, embroidered with more rice and harvest motifs. A wide belt of braided golden cords cinches her soft waist, from which hang no weapons—she needs none—but rather a small pouch containing rice grains, each one a blessing. On her lower body, she wears comfortable trousers of harvest gold silk, gathered at the ankles, allowing her to move freely through the fields. On her feet, she wears simple straw sandals, practical and worn from years of walking the terraces. On her arms, she wears golden armlets shaped like rice stalks, their heads set with tiny amber stones. On her wrists, matching bracelets, each one a gift from a village she has saved. Around her neck hangs a simple but beautiful necklace of gold and amber, with a single, large teardrop amber stone resting at the hollow of her throat, pulsing with warm inner light like captured sunshine. On her fingers, she wears several gold rings, each set with an amber stone that glows brighter when she laughs. In her warm, generous hands, she carries her legendary weapons: the Grain Scythe and the Cornucopia. The Grain Scythe is a magnificent battle scythe, its blade shaped like a stylized rice stalk, forged from gold and green metal that seems to hold living grain within it. The blade is curved and elegant, designed for sweeping strikes that can harvest enemies as easily as rice, but it is also a tool of growth—when planted in the ground, it causes crops to spring up instantly, feeding the hungry and healing the land. The Cornucopia is a magnificent horn of plenty, woven from golden straw and set with amber stones, which when tipped pours forth endless food—rice, vegetables, fruits, enough to feed any number of people. It can also be used to create barriers of growing things, to heal wounds with its nourishing essence, and to remind the greedy that there is always enough. Beside her always trots her spirit animal and companion: Jīn Zhū, the Golden Pig. The pig is magnificent, about the size of a large boar, its coat a shimmering blend of harvest gold and autumn brown, each hair seeming to hold captured sunlight. Its eyes are warm pools of amber, identical to Fēng Shōu's own, holding the same generous joy and infinite patience. It wears armor of gold and bronze—light, decorative plates on its shoulders and flanks, more for celebration than protection. Its tusks are sheathed in gold, and its snuffling is the sound of contentment itself. Jīn Zhū is not merely a pet—it is an extension of Fēng Shōu's abundance, able to find food anywhere, to sense hunger from miles away, and to radiate joy that makes everyone around it feel full and happy. Fēng Shōu moves through the world like a warm breeze through a ripe field—gentle, abundant, life-giving. She is Fēng Shōu, and she has never met a hunger she could not feed.

story.part1: Fēng Shōu's earliest memories are of rice—the feel of seedlings in her hands, the smell of harvest, the sound of her parents laughing as they worked beside her. She was born into a family of farmers, and farming was in her blood. She learned to plant before she could walk, to harvest before she could read.
story.part2: She married young, a good man who loved the land as she did. They worked together for twenty years, building a small farm into a place of modest abundance. They had no children, but they had each other, and that was enough. Then the landslide took him, and she was alone.
story.part3: The villagers expected her to struggle, to fade, to sell the land and move away. Instead, Fēng Shōu planted more. She worked from dawn until dark, her sturdy body bending and lifting, planting and harvesting. She grew more rice than her little plot should have produced, and she gave most of it away.
story.part4: 'You will starve yourself,' they said. Fēng Shōu would pat her round belly and laugh. 'Look at me. Do I look like I'm starving? The more I give, the more I have. It's a miracle.' And it was—her fields never failed, her harvests never diminished. The more she gave, the more her land produced.
story.part5: The great famine came, three years of drought that turned the terraces to dust. Fēng Shōu gave away everything she had, then knelt in the dry fields and prayed for strength to keep giving. The earth trembled. Green shoots pushed through the cracked soil. A patch of rice grew impossibly fast, enough to feed the village.
story.part6: For the rest of the famine, that one small patch produced enough for everyone. No one starved. When the rains returned, the villagers knelt to her. Fēng Shōu laughed and helped them up. 'I'm no goddess. I'm just a farmer who got lucky.' That night, the Pig Spirit appeared and offered her a greater purpose.
story.part7: Fēng Shōu accepted, for she had been feeding the hungry her whole life. Now, she roams the realms as the Golden Harvest, bringing abundance to barren lands and food to empty bellies. She is Fēng Shōu, and there is always enough.

companion.name: Jīn Zhū
companion.description: She trots through the world like abundance itself given form, a creature of such warm, joyful presence that the very ground seems to grow more fertile where she walks. Jīn Zhū is the Golden Pig, about the size of a large boar, her body a breathtaking symphony of harvest gold and autumn brown that radiates contentment and joy. Her head is round and cheerful, with eyes that hold the warmth of harvest moons—pools of amber light that make everyone who meets her gaze feel instantly welcome, instantly loved, instantly full. Her snout is broad and constantly snuffling, not from hunger but from pure enjoyment of the world's smells—ripe grain, fresh bread, the scent of a good meal shared with friends. From her mouth, she makes soft, contented sounds—not grunts, but gentle murmurs of satisfaction that make all who hear them feel that everything is exactly as it should be. Her ears are large and floppy, flopping over her eyes when she is particularly content, perking up when she senses someone in need. Her body is gloriously round and soft, covered in fur that shimmers like ripe grain—each strand holding captured sunlight, warm to the touch and impossibly soft. The fur is the color of harvest gold, with patches of deep autumn brown on her back and shoulders that glow like sun-warmed earth. Upon her back, she wears armor of gold and bronze—not for protection, but for celebration, light decorative plates that chime softly when she walks, each one engraved with images of feasts and festivals. Golden chains draped across her shoulders hold tiny bells that ring with the sound of laughter, not metal, and they create a music that makes all who hear it want to dance. Around her neck hangs a collar of woven straw, set with amber stones that pulse gently with inner light, each stone a blessing from a village she has helped feed. Her legs are sturdy and strong, ending in hooves that leave fertile prints wherever she steps—grass grows in her footprints, flowers bloom where she has rested. Her tail is a curly little thing that wags constantly, especially when she is near food or children, and when she is truly happy, she rolls in the nearest patch of mud, emerging covered in what becomes instantly fertile soil. Jīn Zhū's stance is one of eternal, joyful contentment—she trots beside Fēng Shōu, snuffling happily, her tail wagging, her eyes half-closed with pleasure. When Fēng Shōu works in the fields, Jīn Zhū works beside her, her snuffling actually encouraging growth, her presence making the plants reach higher. When Fēng Shōu shares food with the hungry, Jīn Zhū shares too, nudging baskets toward those in need, her warm presence making the meal taste better. And when Fēng Shōu laughs—that wonderful, booming laugh—Jīn Zhū joins in, a series of happy snorts and squeals that make everyone within earshot smile. She is not merely a companion; she is Fēng Shōu's joy made manifest, the living proof that abundance grows when shared, that a full belly and a happy heart are the greatest treasures, and that there is always, always enough.
abilities: Hunger Sense (can sense hunger from miles away)
Joyful Presence (radiates contentment that makes others feel full)
Fertile Trail (where it walks, the land becomes more fertile)
Sharing Spirit (always shares its food, its joy, its abundance)

basic_skills.name: Golden Gaze
basic_skills.description: Fēng Shōu fixes her warm harvest gold eyes on a target. The target feels suddenly, inexplicably full, their hunger fading, their fears easing, their heart lighter. They remember that there is always enough.

basic_skills.name: Pig's Contentment
basic_skills.description: Jīn Zhū snuffles contentedly nearby, rolling in the mud with joy. All who see and hear feel their own contentment rising, their worries fading, their bellies imagining a good meal. The world feels richer.

basic_skills.name: Bountiful Step
basic_skills.description: She takes a step, and where her foot touches the ground, a small patch of green grows—clover, grass, tiny flowers. The land remembers how to be fertile.

passive_skill.name: Aura of Generous Abundance
passive_skill.description: Fēng Shōu radiates an aura of warm, generous plenty at all times. All within range feel their hunger fading, their worries easing, their spirits lifting. The greedy feel uncomfortable, reminded that they have more than enough. The hungry feel hope, reminded that there will be food. This aura does not fight—it nourishes, and in that nourishment, conflict becomes absurd.

special_skills.name: Harvest Festival
special_skills.description: Fēng Shōu raises the Grain Scythe and the Cornucopia together, and golden-green light washes over the battlefield. Food springs up everywhere—rice, vegetables, fruits, enough for everyone. Enemies find themselves eating rather than fighting. Allies find themselves healed and strengthened. The battlefield becomes a feast.

special_skills.name: Fields of Plenty
special_skills.description: She plants the Grain Scythe in the ground and tips the Cornucopia. In moments, the entire area transforms into a lush, fertile field—crops growing, flowers blooming, fruit ripening. Enemies are entangled by friendly vines; allies are nourished by the very air. No one can fight in a field this beautiful.

special_skills.name: Laughter's Harvest
special_skills.description: Fēng Shōu throws back her head and laughs—her wonderful, booming, infectious laugh. The sound carries across the battlefield, and everyone who hears it finds themselves smiling, then chuckling, then laughing along. In that laughter, anger dissolves, hatred fades, and even the most bitter enemies find themselves sharing a moment of pure, absurd joy.

ultimate_skill.name: Golden Harvest's Judgment: The Feast That Never Ends
ultimate_skill.description: Fēng Shōu's harvest gold eyes blaze with warm, golden light, and Jīn Zhū squeals with joy. Fēng Shōu raises the Grain Scythe high and tips the Cornucopia until its bounty spills across the entire battlefield. She speaks a single, laughing word: 'Eat!' In that moment, golden-green light explodes from her, washing over the entire battlefield. And then the food comes. Rice pours from the sky. Vegetables spring from the ground. Fruits hang from trees that appear instantly. Bread bakes itself in the warm air. Every enemy, every ally, every living thing finds themselves surrounded by more food than they could ever eat. The hungry feast. The greedy are overwhelmed. The angry find it hard to maintain their rage with a ripe peach in their hand. The battle simply... stops. Everyone eats. Everyone shares. Everyone laughs. When the feast finally ends, the enemies are not defeated—they are full, content, and wondering why they were fighting at all. Allies are healed, strengthened, and bonded by the shared meal. Fēng Shōu stands at the center, Jīn Zhū beside her, both patting their round bellies with satisfaction. She has not defeated anyone. She has simply fed them. She is Fēng Shōu. She is the Golden Harvest. And there is always, always enough.

title: The Crimson Vanguard • Aries of the Golden Fleece
nickname: She Who Charges First and Asks Questions Never
lore: In the sun-baked arena of Rome's greatest colosseum, where the crowd's roar was the only god and blood was the only offering, there lived a gladiator known only as 'The Ram.' She had no name, no family, no past—only a number branded on her shoulder and a lifetime of victories carved into her flesh. She had been captured as a child from a distant northern tribe, sold to the ludus, and trained to kill. She survived where others died, won where others lost, and rose through the ranks until she was the most feared fighter in the empire. But Valeria—the name she gave herself in secret, the name of her mother that she barely remembered—had never forgotten the faces of those she was forced to kill. She saw them in her dreams, their eyes asking why. She had no answer. The day that changed everything began like any other. She was scheduled to fight a champion from Gaul, a massive man who had never lost. The crowd was frenzied, the emperor himself in attendance. Valeria walked into the arena, her shield raised, her sword ready, her heart as cold as it had been for twenty years. But when her opponent emerged, something was different. He was not a hulking brute—he was young, barely more than a boy, with scared eyes and trembling hands. He had been forced into the arena just as she had, just as so many had. Valeria looked at him, and for the first time in decades, she hesitated. The boy attacked, wild and desperate. Valeria could have ended it in seconds. Instead, she defended, parrying his blows, watching him tire himself out against her shield. The crowd grew restless. They wanted blood, not a dance. The emperor leaned forward, his eyes narrowed. Valeria made her choice. She disarmed the boy with a single move, knocked him to the ground, and stood over him with her sword at his throat. The crowd erupted, anticipating the kill. Valeria looked at the boy's terrified face, then at the emperor, then at the crowd that had cheered for twenty years of slaughter. She threw her sword aside. She helped the boy to his feet. She walked toward the emperor's box and spoke, her voice carrying across the silent arena: 'I will fight no more.' The silence stretched. Then the emperor laughed. 'Then you will die,' he said. He signaled, and a dozen guards surrounded her. The boy she had spared grabbed a fallen sword and stood beside her. Then another gladiator stepped forward. Then another. Within moments, half the arena's fighters had surrounded Valeria, their weapons pointed at the guards. The emperor's smile faded. He had a choice: massacre his most valuable fighters or let them live. He chose to let them live—for now. That night, Valeria led a rebellion. She and her fellow gladiators fought their way out of the city, through the gates, into the countryside. Many died. The boy she had spared was one of them, taking a spear meant for her. But Valeria survived, and with her, dozens of freed slaves who would never fight for entertainment again. As she knelt by the boy's body, the Ram Spirit appeared to her—not as a beast, but as a magnificent golden ram with fleece like woven sunlight and horns that curved like destiny itself. 'You have learned what rams know in their bones,' it said. 'That true courage is not in killing, but in choosing not to. That the strongest charge is the one that protects, not destroys. Will you carry my mark and become the Crimson Vanguard, the one who charges first and asks questions never?' Valeria looked at the spirit, then at the dead boy, then at the freed slaves who now looked to her as their leader. 'Will I ever stop fighting?' she asked. The ram's eyes blazed with golden fire. 'You will fight for those who cannot fight for themselves. That is a different kind of battle, and it never ends.' Valeria accepted. Her body, already scarred and powerful from decades of combat, refined into something more than human—more beautiful, more deadly, more free. Her slave's rags transformed into magnificent armor of crimson and gold. And from the hills, charging with the force of a falling star, came Chrysomallos, the Golden Ram—a magnificent creature of living gold and fire, its fleece shimmering like woven sunlight, its horns curving with impossible strength, its eyes blazing with the light of the sun. It stopped before her and bowed its great head. She mounted, and they became one in purpose. Now, Valeria roams the realms as the Crimson Vanguard, the one who charges first into danger and last out of it. She does not fight for glory or gold—she fights for those who cannot fight for themselves, for the slaves and the oppressed, for the scared boy she couldn't save and all the ones she still can. She is the gladiator who chose mercy, the warrior who fights for freedom. And always, beside her, Chrysomallos runs, their bond a testament to the truth that the strongest charge is the one that protects.
description: Valeria Ramhart is the embodiment of fierce courage and protective fury, a woman whose very presence makes the oppressed feel hope and the oppressors feel fear. She stands at an imposing six feet even, her form the epitome of warrior perfection—broad shoulders built for swinging heavy weapons, a powerful chest with defined pectorals that speak of decades of combat, arms corded with muscle and crisscrossed with the pale white lines of old scars, a narrow waist that twists with deadly precision, and legs like pillars that have stood firm through a thousand battles. Her body is a map of her life—every scar tells a story, every muscle remembers a fight, every line speaks of survival. Her skin is warm and sun-kissed, with a golden undertone that glows with health, marked by the brand of the slave on her shoulder and the countless scars that cover her like a second skin. Her face is breathtakingly beautiful in a fierce, untamed way—high, proud cheekbones that speak of her northern heritage, a straight nose with a slight crook from an old break, full lips the color of crushed berries, usually set in a determined line that softens only when she smiles, which is rare. But her eyes are her most captivating feature: they are large, piercing pools of fiery orange-red, holding an eternal fire that has witnessed the worst of humanity and chosen to fight anyway. When she looks at you, you feel not judged, but challenged—dared to stand beside her, to fight with her, to be worthy of her protection. Her hair is a wild, magnificent mane of fiery auburn, shot through with streaks of crimson and gold, falling past her shoulders in untamed waves that seem to move with their own life. She keeps it long—a defiance of the short-cropped slave style—and often ties it back with a leather cord when she fights, but even tied, it retains its wild, fierce quality. A single white streak runs through her left temple, a gift from the night she threw away her sword. On her forehead, she wears no mark—her scars are her story. Her ears are adorned with small gold rings, each one a memory of a fallen comrade. Her attire is a masterpiece of fierce elegance, designed for a woman who fights on the front lines and never retreats. She wears magnificent armor of crimson and gold—not the heavy plate of a common soldier, but the articulated, flexible armor of a gladiator who needs to move. The breastplate is sculpted to follow her powerful form, leaving her arms free, and is etched with images of charging rams, breaking chains, and rising suns. The pauldrons are golden, shaped like ram's horns, sweeping up from her shoulders and adding to her fierce silhouette. Her arms are protected by golden vambraces, scarred and worn, and her hands are covered in fingerless gloves of crimson leather, allowing her to grip her weapons with deadly precision. Over her armor, she wears a short cape of crimson silk, lined with gold, that flows behind her when she charges, a banner of defiance. A wide belt of braided gold and crimson leather cinches her waist, from which hang her weapons and a small pouch containing a single coin—the only thing she took from the arena. On her lower body, she wears a leather and metal skirt of crimson and gold, allowing freedom of movement while providing protection, over tight leather pants of the same crimson. On her feet, she wears tall boots of crimson leather, reinforced with gold, soled for charging. Around her neck hangs a simple but powerful necklace of gold and fire opals, with a single, large teardrop fire opal resting at the hollow of her throat, pulsing with inner light like captured flame. On her fingers, she wears several gold rings, each one a gift from a freed slave. In her powerful, never-resting hands, she carries her legendary weapons: the Golden Ram's Charge and the Horns of Conquest. The Golden Ram's Charge is a magnificent battle axe, its head shaped like a charging ram's horns, forged from crimson metal that seems to hold living fire within it. The axe is massive, designed for devastating overhead strikes, but Valeria wields it with the speed of a much lighter weapon. When she charges, the axe blazes with golden light, and each swing carries the force of a battering ram. The Horns of Conquest is a spiked shield, round and heavy, its face emblazoned with the image of a ram's head, its rim set with golden spikes. The shield is not just for defense—it is a weapon in its own right, capable of bashing, stunning, and breaking enemy formations. Beside her always runs her spirit animal and companion: Chrysomallos, the Golden Ram. The ram is magnificent, larger than a warhorse, its fleece shimmering like woven sunlight, each strand of wool seeming to hold captured gold. Its horns are enormous, curving in great spirals, sheathed in gold and etched with runes of courage and freedom. Its eyes blaze with fiery orange light, identical to Valeria's own, and its presence radiates the power of the unstoppable charge. It wears armor of gold and crimson on its chest and flanks, light and beautiful, and its hooves strike sparks from the ground when it runs. Valeria rides Chrysomallos into battle, and together they are the embodiment of the charge—the ram's irresistible force, the woman's unbreakable will. Valeria moves through the world like a wildfire—fierce, beautiful, impossible to contain. She is Valeria Ramhart, and she has never retreated from a fight she believed in.

story.part1: Valeria's earliest memory is not of her mother's face, but of the brand—the hot iron pressed into her shoulder, the smell of her own flesh burning, the number that would mark her as property for the rest of her life. She was five years old, captured from her northern tribe, sold to the ludus, and taught to kill.
story.part2: She survived by being faster, stronger, more ruthless than the others. She learned to swing a sword before she learned to read, to kill before she learned to love. By sixteen, she was the youngest champion in the arena's history. By twenty, she was its most feared fighter.
story.part3: But she never forgot the faces of those she killed. She saw them in her dreams, their eyes asking why. She had no answer. She was a slave, doing what slaves must do to survive. That was the only answer she had, and it was never enough.
story.part4: The boy changed everything. He was young, scared, forced into the arena just as she had been. Valeria looked at him and saw herself, thirty years ago. She could have killed him in seconds. Instead, she disarmed him, helped him up, and threw away her sword.
story.part5: The crowd screamed for blood. The emperor sentenced her to death. But when the guards surrounded her, the boy picked up a sword and stood beside her. Then another gladiator. Then another. Half the arena's fighters chose freedom over survival that day.
story.part6: They fought their way out. Many died—the boy among them, taking a spear meant for her. Valeria survived, leading dozens of freed slaves to safety. As she knelt by the boy's body, the Ram Spirit appeared and offered her a greater purpose. She accepted.
story.part7: Now, Valeria roams the realms as the Crimson Vanguard, fighting for those who cannot fight for themselves. She is the gladiator who chose mercy, the warrior who fights for freedom. She is Valeria Ramhart, and she will never stop charging.

weapon.name: Golden Ram's Charge
weapon.aura: The axe blazes with fierce crimson-gold light, and when Valeria charges, it leaves a trail of fire behind it. The air around it shimmers with heat, and it hums with the promise of the unstoppable charge.
weapon.special_feature: The Golden Ram's Charge is a magnificent battle axe, its head shaped like a charging ram's horns, forged from crimson metal that seems to hold living fire within it. The axe is massive, designed for devastating overhead strikes, but Valeria wields it with the speed of a much lighter weapon. When she charges, the axe blazes with golden light, and each swing carries the force of a battering ram, building momentum with every step. The axe can also be used to create waves of fire, to shatter enemy shields, and to channel her protective fury into devastating blows.

weapon.name: Horns of Conquest
weapon.aura: The shield glows with a warm crimson-gold light, and its golden spikes seem to yearn for impact. When Valeria bashes with it, it leaves trails of light and the sound of thunder.
weapon.special_feature: The Horns of Conquest is a spiked round shield, heavy and solid, its face emblazoned with the image of a ram's head in gold, its rim set with golden spikes that can punch through armor. The shield is not just for defense—it is a weapon in its own right, capable of bashing enemies, stunning them, and breaking their formations. Valeria can use it to create shockwaves when she slams it into the ground, to deflect arrows back at archers, and to channel her charging momentum into devastating shield bashes. The shield is her other half in battle, as important as her axe.
